accounts.name: guardian
docs: Optional guardian PDA tied to `signer` via PDA seeds (no spoofing).
Required when signer != admin. FIX B: a guardian can kill a malicious
admin-transfer proposal during the 24h delay window.

instructions.name: cancel_guardian_removal
docs: Cancels a scheduled removal. Admin OR the targeted guardian itself.

accounts.name: guardian
docs: Optional guardian PDA tied to `signer` via PDA seeds (no spoofing). Required when signer != admin.

accounts.name: recipient_ata
docs: Recipient USDC ATA. Owner is asserted manually in handler against action_data.recipient.
Anchor `token::authority` constraint cannot reference action_data, so we deserialize
and check manually with a dedicated error.

instructions.name: finalize_guardian_removal
docs: Applies a scheduled removal after its window. Permissionless on purpose.

accounts.name: guardian
docs: Optional guardian PDA tied to `signer` via PDA seeds. Required when signer != admin.
The seeds constraint forces the PDA to belong to the signer (no spoofing).

instructions.name: remove_guardian
docs: AUDIT 0.12b: SCHEDULES a removal (does not apply it). The guardian keeps
full powers for admin_timelock_seconds and may cancel its own removal, so a
compromised admin can no longer clear the veto in one signature.

accounts.name: silv_mint
docs: Read-only, pinned to the configured SILV mint so the supply cannot be
spoofed by passing a different mint.

fields.name: cancelled_pending_admin
docs: The admin-elect whose handover was just cancelled. None is impossible in
practice (the handler requires a pending transfer) but the field is an
Option so the event cannot lie if that ever changes.

types.name: DevParamSet
docs: SC-M7: dev-only handler audit trail. Emitted on dev_set_max_staleness
and dev_set_premiums calls so devnet operators have a log of what
changed and when. param: 1 = max_staleness_seconds, 2 = premiums.
value_a/value_b are the new values (interpretation depends on param).

types.name: InventoryWalletChanged
docs: SolidProof MEDIUM #3 asked specifically for this one: the pre-mint destination
can be redirected instantly, so the redirect must at least be observable.

fields.name: live_supply
docs: Live mint supply at the moment of the change, so the "how much headroom
was just removed" question is answerable from the log alone.

types.name: RedeemLimitsTightened
docs: The instant tighten fast lane. Every field is Option in the args, so the event
reports the resulting values rather than only what was supplied.
